prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study asks whether the need for the RIM scaffold protein is the same for all synapses that have different natural release probabilities.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Researchers used a neurotoxin to block specific nerve inputs in fruit flies to test how the RIM protein affects different synapses.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The RIM protein is strictly necessary for nerve signals to pass at one type of synapse but is not needed at a nearby synapse of a different type.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The need for RIM also depends on the type of long-term change: it is required for rapid adjustments at the high-probability synapse but not for slow adjustments at the low-probability synapse.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: High-resolution images show that the RIM protein sits physically closer to calcium channels at the synapse that releases neurotransmitters more frequently.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: During rapid changes in activity, RIM helps rearrange calcium channels at a tiny scale to increase the number of vesicles ready for release.
facts.subject: animals
